body:
_Migrated from issue #1353, filed 2026-08-04._

Found by the v4.1.29 pre-tag refuter gate. Narrow, but it is the same bug class #1343 fixed
from the other direction, re-entering through the savepoint added in this release.

## The hole

`cps/services/reading_position.py` `record_web_reader_progress` wraps
`update_book_read_status` in `ub.session.begin_nested()` — a SAVEPOINT on **app.db**.

At ≥99% with `config_read_column` set, that call reaches `_mark_custom_read_column`
(`kosync.py:522`), which runs its own unconditional `calibre_db.session.commit()` — an
independent commit to a **different database**, metadata.db.

If the savepoint then rolls back — precisely the racing-writer `IntegrityError` the savepoint
exists to absorb — metadata.db is committed "read" while app.db's `ReadBook` write is undone.
The two read-status carriers diverge, which is exactly what #1343 was about.

Needs custom read column + ≥99% + a real race, so it is narrow. But note the savepoint is what
*creates* the window: on the kosync path a failure propagates instead of silently discarding
half the work.

## Fix direction

Move `_mark_custom_read_column` outside the savepoint, or defer it until after the outer commit
succeeds, so the cross-database write only happens once the app.db side is durable.

## Second, pre-existing item found alongside

`kobo_statistics` has no uniqueness constraint, and the live DB already carries a duplicate
(`kobo_reading_state_id=17` → 2 rows), producing
`SAWarning: Multiple rows returned with uselist=False for 'KoboReadingState.statistics'`.
Pre-existing, but `_ensure_visible_reading_state` is now on the web-reader path and therefore
runs far more often than it used to, so the duplicate is easier to hit.
title: Web-reader savepoint can roll back app.db while metadata.db stays committed
